lesson-2.says: A run-row field that is always present with a default is one entry in `RUN_FIELDS` (`lib/dispatch-fields.js`). A sparse field stays a conditional spread in `addItem` and `_archiveItem`, so other rows keep their key sets byte-identical. Six fields were once dropped on one hop of four.

lesson-3.says: Every exit from the queue except a take archives through `_archiveItem` (`lib/dispatch-store.js`); a new exit must archive through it too.

lesson-4.says: The wake path is `_planWake` (decide) then `_deliverWake` (deliver) in `lib/dispatch-store.js`, shared by `addFeedback` and the held-wake release (LIN-4373). Its guards (LIN-1059, 1165, 1357, 2297, 4080, 4166) run in an order that matters: change the pair whole, keep the wake suites passing, and update the two census pins (`lin-3134-declared-mint-census`, `lin-4080-addItem-census`) if the write moves.

lesson-5.says: "This run's PR" is the session's own report: `prUrlOfFeedback` (`lib/dispatch-wake.js`) takes a PR on a report line before the `[done]` `url`, which older runners filled by mention count (LIN-4375).

lesson-6.says: Two `[done]` posts can reach a decide-then-enqueue at once, so "no row yet" is no guard: claim first, compare-and-set on the row (`claimHeldWake`). LIN-4373 relied on the read and queued two leftover rows (LIN-4375).

lesson-7.says: A claim whose holder skips is released on every path out (`releaseHeldWakeClaim`). A stamp left by a skip held the re-report forever (LIN-4375 review).

lesson-8.says: Any session can park `[pending]` on CI and finish on a ci-wake `custom` row (`lib/ci-wake-sweep.js`). A rule keyed on the producing kind misses that ending: read the lineage (`heldWakeHolderOf`, `resolveFollowUpRoot`). LIN-4373 covered eligibility, not the held wake's terminals.

lesson-9.says: Row-only kinds stay out of `DISPATCH_KINDS` (`lib/prompt-templates.js`) and sit in `ROW_ONLY_KINDS` (`lib/dispatch-fields.js`); kind-keyed maps are tested against both. A new bucket can pull a kind into the round-trip walk, which `OFF_SPINE_KINDS` stops (LIN-4376).

lesson-10.says: The store knows no leftovers (LIN-4383). It holds a parent wake by `heldWakeFor` (LIN-4373), released by the holder's terminal or `_archiveItem` under the build's guard key, so it wakes once. Leftover wording lives in `lib/dispatch-leftover-hook.js`; a new held-wake feature brings a hook (`lin-4377-store-knows-no-leftover` counts the word).

lesson-11.says: Price a pulled extra like any piece: a cost read that rode along with LIN-4201 landed alone as LIN-4226.

lesson-12.says: A task timeline lane is running from the page's open session ids (`isOpenState`), never the cost row; a lineage's own `incomplete`, not the shared `lineagesTruncated`, decides "not complete" (LIN-4405, `lib/task-timeline.js`).

lesson-13.says: A test that dispatches a close-out passes a `closeOut` seam (`resolveProvider`): the readiness guard reads comments for every close-out since LIN-4438, and without the seam it reaches the real provider and fails open, a pass the hermetic watcher catches only in CI.

lesson-14.says: Close-out readiness has five lanes: the route (`codeRouteOf`), the stop-at state, the task page's box (`buildRunEvidence`) and both guard lanes (`closeOutNotReady`). A readiness rule goes in `closeOutWaitsOn` (`lib/run-closeout-state.js`) and gets a row in the shared-trail table (`lin-4438-blind-read-gate`); gating one lane let the page offer a press the guard refused (LIN-4438).

lesson-15.says: A reader that classifies by kind routes `custom` before `bucketOf`: `BUCKET_OF_KIND` maps `custom` to orchestration, and `bucketOf` falls back to orchestration silently, so check membership (`lib/wall-clock-summary.js`). `dispatchesOf` turns a missing kind into `custom` (`lib/cost-read.js`): confirm a custom kind from its own row before trusting it (LIN-4426).

lesson-16.says: A full PR URL's repository and number come from `prOf` beside `prUrlsIn` (`lib/run-ledger.js`), for the task page and measure 1 alike; compare repositories case-blind, as GitHub does (LIN-4439).

lesson-17.says: A per-dispatch figure (its model, cost or completeness) is the fold's answer, carried through `lib/cost-read.js`; a reader never re-ranks `byModel` itself. `dispatchModelOf` in `lib/task-timeline.js` did, and a lane can now name two models. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

finding-22.says: Waiting 5: `lib/dispatch-store.js`: `addFeedback` takes one `wakeHook`; a second held-wake feature first needs composable hooks. (Operator, LIN-4377.)

finding-24.says: Waiting 7: `lib/runner-kit/contract.json`: no row pins a follow-up to a finished, unhalted session (rows cover pause and stop), though the leftover step resumes its build that way (`lib/dispatch-leftover.js`). finding-25.says: Waiting 8: `lib/dispatch-factory.js`: tests `provider.name === 'linear'` beside `isHermeticTestToken` for a test-only transport. (LIN-4347.)

finding-26.says: Waiting 9: `lib/cost-read.js`: split out `readCalls` and `callsSurfaceOf`; settle whether instance-wide reads sit beside workspace-keyed stores. (Survey tally: LIN-4201.)

finding-27.says: Waiting 10: `lib/session-summary.js`: do stored run paragraphs keep pre-cutover figures? (Survey tally: LIN-4201.)

finding-28.says: Waiting 11: `lib/dispatch-feedback-validation.js`: feedback kinds lack one declaration with their role: `PARKED_WAIT_SKIPPED_KINDS` (`lib/session-telemetry.js`), `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`, `findWakeEvent`'s skip rule. (Survey tally: LIN-4240, 4239, 4233.)

finding-29.says: Waiting 12: `lib/wake-shadow.js`: one wake policy, from the LIN-3257 classifier this shadow records. (Survey tally: LIN-3257.)

finding-30.says: Waiting 13: `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`: the per-message transcript fold is here and in SD; one shared fold would turn a transcript into requests. (Survey tally: LIN-4203, LIN-4195.)

finding-31.says: Waiting 14: `lib/recent-runs.js`: `runFact` reads only the row's feedback: a stage parked `[pending]` whose lineage ends `[blocked]` or `[skipped]` reads `running` and holds the live-stage wait until aborted. (LIN-4392.)

finding-32.says: Waiting 15: `lib/run-ledger.js`: `landingPrUrls` counts every full PR URL after its anchor, so it disagrees with the other landing readers in two cases the shared-trail table pins as chosen, not designed (`tests/unit/lin-4438-blind-read-gate.test.js` rows 14 and 15): an audit report that re-cites a merged landing PR puts it in the notes PR's landing (`auditAfterLandingCloseOut` in `lib/recommendation-facts.js` treats only the new PR as the notes PR), and a foreign PR cited before the first review joins a first landing. Each costs a read that must name an extra PR. One comment classifier and one landing reader would make both follow from one rule. A third case is not pinned: an agent's own note (first line `autopilot`, `plan posted`, `plan revised`, or `revision N`) that cites a new PR after review joins `landingPrUrls` but not `isLandingEvidence` (`lib/recommendation-facts.js`), so `blindReadStep` offers a blind read naming a PR the approved review never covered, where a plain note sends it back to review (reproduced at e2d4659c4; Seams & Tangles, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/seams-tangles-review-2026-11-13-run12.md`, §3.0a). (LIN-4438; Survey global on LIN-4438.)

finding-33.says: Waiting 16 (added in cfd152fa4 by LIN-4453's leftover; not among the plan's 20): `lib/run-ledger.js`: `landingPrUrls` skips only blind reads and survey reports, so a comment headed `## Area read` that names a full PR URL would join the ticket's landing. Only the prose rule in `docs/plans/survey/area-read.md` (cite `path@sha`, never a PR URL) keeps the LIN-4447 area reads out today. An area-read kind in the one comment classifier (LIN-4458, piece 2) would make that rule code. (Leftover of LIN-4453; Survey global on LIN-4453.)

finding-34.says: Waiting 17 (the plan's Waiting 16): `lib/run-closeout-state.js`: `deriveCloseOutState` works from two PR lists: `prs` (`extractPrUrls`, every PR ever cited) drives the PR-shape reasons (multiple-prs, partial, merged) and `landingPrs` (`landingPrUrls`) drives the blind-read gate, so the box can count PRs the gate ignores and the other way round (pinned in `tests/unit/lin-4438-blind-read-gate.test.js` rows 14 and 15). Which reader answers "this task's PRs" spans the box, the guard and the route. (Blind read on LIN-4439.)

finding-35.says: Waiting 18 (the plan's Waiting 17): `lib/close-out-readiness.js`: in the stop-at lane `deriveCloseOutState` lets merged and partial outrank the gate, then `closeOutNotReady` asks `closeOutWaitsOn` again to override it, so the box state is not the guard's whole answer and the precedence lives in two files. Carrying the gate's answer in the state changes the box model the renderers read. (Blind read on LIN-4439.) `ladderNotReady` asks the gate a third time, so the box and the guard order the same reasons two ways and the next close-out reason must be placed in both; one order is a decision about what the box shows versus what the guard refuses. (Blind read on LIN-4396.)

finding-36.says: Waiting 19 (the plan's Waiting 18): `lib/run-closeout-state.js`: the close-out reasons are bare string literals: `'blind-read-missing'` is spelled here and again in `REFUSED_REASONS` (`lib/close-out-readiness.js`, beside `'head-moved'`), and `closeOutNotReadyRefusal` builds its error by capitalising `state.message`. A reasons constant (like `CLOSE_OUT_STATUS`) covering every reason, used by the box, the guard and the render, would give them one vocabulary. (Blind read on LIN-4396.)

finding-37.says: Waiting 20 (the plan's Waiting 19): `lib/task-timeline.js`: `dispatchModelOf` picks a dispatch's model by its own rule (`costUsd`, null as -1, then request count), while the home, `foldRequestUsage` (`lib/request-usage-fold.js`), ranks by priced dollars, then latest use, and names the latest model when nothing is priced. `modelRowOf` (`lib/cost-read.js`) drops `pricedUsd`, so the lane label (`session.model`, the fold's answer) and the rows inside it can name different models whenever any request is unpriced. The fix is for `dispatchesOf` to carry the fold's `last.model`; a change to the dominant-model rule otherwise leaves the timeline behind. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov.; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

finding-38.says: Waiting 21 (the plan's Waiting 20): `lib/run-closeout-state.js`: `closeOutSetsDone` never asks `closeOutWaitsOn`, so the owner's check (`routes/workspace-api-run-evidence.js`) sets a stop-at-PR task Done when its landing PR is merged and approved with no blind read, while the close-out guard (`lib/close-out-readiness.js`) refuses the same trail as `blind-read-missing`, and `blindReadStep` (`lib/recommendation-blind-read.js`) then routes a read to the Done ticket (it stands aside on a completed ticket only after a close-out). The entries above name the box/guard precedence split; this is its Done path. Whether a person's own check may pass the gate is a decision; the shared-trail test runs with `byPersonCheck: false`, so it never reaches this path. (Drift & Coherence Review, 13 Nov., second read; `docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-13.md`.)

task-39.asked:
**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** John: "we've not been applying quite the right force to bend the curve… now want to run both real work, and some real tidies." The Drift & Coherence and Seams & Tangles reviews of 13 Nov found this area carrying rules written in two places that disagree. Batch 1 added several of them:

* Harbour can mark a task Done on a person's check before its blind read, while another check refuses that same task, and a read is then sent to a ticket that's already Done (Drift run 7, `close-out-gate-precedence-split`). John's ruling: "if I choose to do something, Harbour is a passenger. This reflects that for many real projects, they're unlikely to be exclusively changed via Harbour."
* Two pieces of code decide which PRs belong to a task, and they disagree about agent notes, so a blind read can be offered over a PR no review covered (Seams run 12, §3.0a).
* The task timeline decides which model a dispatch used by its own rule, separate from the one the cost figures use (Drift, row 150).
* The check that makes a stage wait while another is live is a runs rule, but it lives with the prompts (Seams, P-LW1).

The area's note holds 20 Waiting entries, and `lib/dispatch-store.js` is 4,530 lines. Seams also tried moving files between areas three ways, and none made the tangle smaller.

**What we want.**

* Each rule in the area has one home, and the copies are gone.
* When a person acts, Harbour follows, and that rule is written once.
* The area's Waiting entries are settled, or each says why it can't be yet.
* Each piece finishes one move and names what it retired. John: "I'd be happy to run a small variety, erring larger, to see", so piece sizes vary, leaning larger.
* The LLM & prompts side of the seam is A14's.

**Done when**

* the cases above are settled, or John has ruled they can wait;
* the area's Waiting entries are settled or say why not;
* the area reads better in a blind read after this work than before it, by more than an untouched area read at the same times.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

finding-67.says: `wakeHook.releaseNote` cannot reach most held-wake releases. The hook is built per request (`leftoverStep.forRequest`, `routes/dispatch.js:1636`, `routes/proxy-runner.js:213`) and passed only into `addFeedback`; most releases go `_archiveItem` -> `_releaseIfHeld` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:1890`, `:1949`) from `removeItem`, `cleanup()` expiry and stopped-run cleanup, none of which holds a request or hook; only the `_applyWakeHook` re-release (`:3429`) does. Put the wording on `leftoverStep` and late-bind it into the store the way `setWakeCredentialProvisionerFactory` is (`server.js:1146`). Decide what an unbound store says: `lin-4373-leftover-step.test.js` asserts "did not run" five times. This is a second hook surface, the thing Waiting 5 (finding-22, one `wakeHook`) warns about, so shape it with that in mind. Do this first: it is the only part that changes the store shape, and it fixes what the rewritten lin-4377 witness counts (no `formatHeldWakeNote` import in the store).

question-68.asks: Plan piece 5 puts the one `FEEDBACK_KINDS` table in `lib/dispatch-feedback-validation.js`. That file imports `dispatch-validation.js`, which reaches `session-telemetry.js` (prompt-templates -> ... -> wall-clock-summary) and `dispatch-terminal.js` (dispatch-fields -> dispatch-wake); if those import the table and build Sets from it at load, load order decides whether they hit a TDZ error. May the table live in a new import-free leaf instead, with validation and the store importing it and the store still re-exporting `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`?
options: keep the plan: table in lib/dispatch-feedback-validation.js
new leaf module lib/dispatch-feedback-kinds.js with no imports
question-68.recommended: new leaf module lib/dispatch-feedback-kinds.js with no imports
question-68.if-unanswered: implementation builds the leaf module (an engineering call) and the PR says it departs from plan-45 on the table home

finding-69.says: `findWakeEvent` has no skip rule to derive. It returns the last matching marker of any kind (`lib/dispatch-terminal.js:631`), and `lib/session-telemetry.js:82` calls it "Deliberately NOT shared". Deriving a filter would change the mint path (`lib/dispatch-store.js:3696`) and every reader of stored rows (task-page-loader, run-view, digest-feedback, run-loop-state), against "never recompute pre-cutover history". Record its role as a table column ("every kind may carry a wake") and pin that current behaviour matches it, rather than add a filter. The done-when says "`findWakeEvent`'s skip rule derive from it"; the PR should say it is met by the column, not a filter.

finding-70.says: Prompt seam: `lib/prompts/runner-kickoff.js` (A14 / LIN-4448's side) renders `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` into the runner prompt in its current order, checked by `runner-kickoff.test.js:191`; a derived list must keep that exact order, so add a test that `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` keeps it. The table also needs rows for kinds deliberately not on the allowlist (`decision-answer`, `decision-withdrawal-reversed`; see `DECISION_LIFECYCLE_STAMP_KINDS`, `lib/session-telemetry.js:60`); without them a roles column quietly widens what the runner may post.

finding-72.says: A second reason for question-68's leaf: `lib/dispatch-feedback-validation.js:13` imports its kind list from the store, so the dependency already points the wrong way. Putting the `FEEDBACK_KINDS` table in validation means the store imports validation for a table validation now imports from the store: a direct cycle, not only the TDZ risk through `dispatch-validation.js`. A leaf `lib/dispatch-feedback-kinds.js` that imports nothing, with the store keeping its re-export, removes both.
